Mina / Ben — reviewed the redlines in Cedarbridge_Redlines.docx. High-level legal assessment: this set of changes is outside our delegated authority and materially increases Redwood's downstream risk. Key items of concern:

1) Liability cap removal: Removing the liability ceiling removes our predictable exposure model. For a customer of this size, unlimited exposure for IP or data-related claims could be catastrophic — estimated worst-case exposure (litigation + regulatory) could exceed $12M.

2) Indemnity expansion: They want indemnity for regulatory fines and regulatory enforcement tied to customer misuse. Indemnifying fines for a customer's non-compliant use of their own systems exposes us to regulatory penalties (HIPAA-like scenarios) — we cannot accept that as-is.

3) 36-month warranty + SLA carve-out: Extended warranty period increases bug-fix and maintenance obligations. SLA credits unbounded will create large credit risk.

Options for escalation (recommendations):
- Preferred commercial compromise: keep a liability cap set at 2x annual fees with an IP carve-out for willful infringement (and 3x for negotiated strategic exceptions). Keep indemnity for third-party IP claims but expressly exclude statutory fines, punitive damages, and customer regulatory non-compliance. Limit warranty extension to 18 months for critical security fixes only.
- If leadership decides to make an exception for Cedarbridge (strategic partnership), require: (a) an upfront one-time professional-services payment to offset risk; (b) escrow for source for a limited remediation right; (c) a structured indemnity with sub-limits and an audit right.

I have annotated the redlines in the attached DOCX. This requires signoff from the CPO/CFO/CEO group — legal does not have authority to accept unlimited indemnity or cap removal.

Marissa Cole

Karthik / Laura — forwarding for leadership decision. TL;DR: Cedarbridge (life sciences company) will pause procurement unless we remove our liability cap for IP/data claims and accept their expanded indemnity. They also want a 45% first-year discount. Losing them would delay a larger partnership scheduled for Q2 that could be $3.5M ARR in year two.

What I'm asking for: a single-point decision from the leadership committee today or tomorrow. Options I will present if you want to delegate:
A) Approve with guardrails (recommended by Legal): cap at 2x fees, exclude statutory fines, require PS uplift and escrow clause; accept 40% discount.
B) Approve limited concession: maintain cap but accept 30% discount and 18-month warranty for critical security patches only.
C) Walk: decline redlines and offer a firm standard contract with 20% discount; risk losing the account.

Impact summaries (numbers):
- Revenue: 45% discount → first-year ARR ~$660k; 40% → ~$720k; 20% (standard) → ~$960k.
- Risk exposure: unlimited/no-cap → theoretical exposure >$12M; proposed cap (2x fees) → exposure bounded to ~$2.4M.

If you want a short one-pager for the exec packet I can draft it (1 page, decision + recommended language) and route for signature. Please reply with APPROVE-A / APPROVE-B / DECLINE by EOD 12/13 so I can communicate to Cedarbridge procurement.
